messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 INCIDENT: Elevated SRV lookup errors observed for service=redis-cluster in us-east-2a. Alerts: 47% SRV NXDOMAIN over 5m. Runbook: https://runbooks.internal/srv-lookup-failure
amal (on-call): acked. looking now. paging pagerduty -> amal
jake: on it, amal — can you confirm if this is CoreDNS or Consul sided? any obvious logs?
amal (on-call): initial glance: CoreDNS pods in us-east-2a reporting repeated "lookup redis-cluster.service.consul. SRV: no such host". consul agents show raft peers 4/5 then drop to 2/5 in that AZ window
taylor: FYI we had a minor maintenance window earlier in us-east-2a for a VRF migration at 02:00Z. did not touch consul nodes but network paths changed.
susan (support): support channel getting customer reports: error from app: "service discovery failed: NXDOMAIN" — a handful of high-traffic tenants hitting cache misses and falling back to reduced capacity. Impact: degraded for ~15% of redis traffic in that AZ.
lin: sharing quick command output (from node consul-3): ```
# consul operator raft list-peers
Node      ID                                   Addr             State
consul-1  abcd1234-... 10.10.32.11:8300  leader
consul-2  bcde2345-... 10.10.33.12:8300  follower
consul-3  cdef3456-... 10.10.34.13:8300  follower
consul-4  def45678-... 10.10.35.14:8300  left
consul-5  efgh5678-... 10.10.36:15:8300  left
```
lin: looks like two peers flapped/leaving around 02:18Z in that AZ, causing read inconsistencies for SRV queries proxied through Consul catalog.
amal (on-call): mitigation plan: 1) avoid aggressive negative caching in CoreDNS for consul domain 2) force consul retry to quorum or route SRV queries to healthy proxies 3) rolling restart of CoreDNS in us-east-2a to clear NXDOMAIN caches. will coordinate.
jake: +1 — do the CoreDNS restart first (low risk) and watch for resolution. prepare fallback to route traffic across AZ if not fixed in 8m.
amal (on-call): running: `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/coredns --selector=zone=us-east-2a` — doing in small batches (2 pods)
... (rolling restart logs) ...
logan: deploy-bot: rollout started for deployment/coredns in us-east-2a, batch=1/3
amal (on-call): after first batch: cache eviction visible, some SRV lookups now return correct records again. metrics: SRV error rate down to 22% -> 8%
taylor: while this is happening, i'm going to patch coredns config to reduce negative ttl for consul domain: `consul { ttl 5s }` — will apply on restart. putting patch now.
amal (on-call): patch applied and second batch restarted. monitoring.
lin: also bumped consul gossip retransmit and forced leader reelection on healthy nodes: ```
# consul operator raft remove-peer def45678-...
# consul debug-raft-force-leader consul-1
```
jake: are we seeing cross-AZ routing flaps? any network ACLs?
taylor: checked VPC flow logs — some intermittent RSTs seen from nodepool subnets to consul ports at 02:17-02:20Z, corresponds to the maintenance VRF change. suspect transient asymmetric routing causing TLS sessions to drop and consul agents to mark peers left.
susan (support): customer impact notes: about 12 tenants reported reduced throughput, most auto-recovered after ~6 minutes as caches warmed or clients retried. recording timeline for postmortem.
claire: product asks whether any requests were permanently lost or if this was transient with retries — also flagging top affected customers so we can reach out proactively.
amal (on-call): handoff note: I'm going offline for 30m at 03:05Z — jake will take primary oncall. summary: CoreDNS negative caching + Consul peer flaps tied to VRF migration -> rolling restarts + consul leader fixes mitigated.
jake: taking over. monitoring retention: watch SRV error rate, consul raft health, and client error traces for next 60m.
(20m later)
amal (on-call): quick update before leaving: overall SRV error rate back to baseline (0.5% noisy neighbors). Consul raft stable 5/5. CoreDNS caches evicted, negative-ttl lowered temporarily.
claire: thanks — product wants postmortem and a one-pager for affected customers, pls include timeline and mitigation steps.
lin: immediate action items logged: [INC-1965] revert VRF change if recurrence, add pre-checks for consul/gossip before network switchover, and alert tuning for SRV NXDOMAIN spikes.
jake: created incident ticket and assigned follow-ups. will add config diff and logs. declaring incident: monitoring -> stable, no active customer escalations.
deploy-bot: Incident marked stable by jake at 1965432389
claire: please add action: disable long negative cache for consul.* in CoreDNS default config and add a synthetic probe that exercises SRV lookups across AZs every 30s.
amal (on-call): added that to follow-ups. i'll draft the postmortem with timeline and root cause hypothesis: transient network path change -> consul peer drop -> CoreDNS cached NXDOMAIN -> client retries/partial failures.
jake: thanks team. if anything reappears ping pagerduty -> oncall. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
